raw_findings.body: Group resources in V2 are named by group ID (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returning group.getId()), while getId() is the authz Resource's own UUID. hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) therefore never finds the per-group resource (findByName with a resource UUID returns null) and falls back to the all-groups check, and granted collects resource UUIDs rather than group IDs. Callers store this set in session attribute UserModel.GROUPS / pass it to getUsersCount, where the JPA group-membership subquery matches nothing — user counts return 0 and group-scoped searches return no users (or all groups' resource UUIDs when an all-groups policy exists), inconsistent with per-user canView evaluation.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Admins with per-group view-members/manage-members permissions get zero user counts and empty group-filtered user searches despite having access.
raw_findings.impact: Group resources in V2 are named by group ID (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returning group.getId()), while getId() is the authz Resource's own UUID. hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) therefore never finds the per-group resource (findByName with a resource UUID returns null) and falls back to the all-groups check, and granted collects resource UUIDs rather than group IDs. Callers store this set in session attribute UserModel.GROUPS / pass it to getUsersCount, where the JPA group-membership subquery matches nothing — user counts return 0 and group-scoped searches return no users (or all groups' resource UUIDs when an all-groups policy exists), inconsistent with per-user canView evaluation.
raw_findings.root_cause: Confusion between the authz Resource's generated ID and the Resource's name, which is the group ID in the V2 schema.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use groupResource.getName() (which holds the group ID) both as the argument to hasPermission(...) and as the value added to the granted set.
raw_findings.title: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes/collects authz resource IDs instead of group IDs
raw_findings.trigger: With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, an admin without global view-users permission is granted VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on a specific group, then calls a user count or search endpoint (UsersResource.getUsersCount / searchForUser, BruteForceUsersResource) that relies on getGroupIdsWithViewPermission().

raw_findings.body: canManage() returns true when only the VIEW scope is granted because the hasPermission check accepts either scope, so a view-only admin can pass manage checks (e.g. create groups) — a privilege escalation. Compare canManage(GroupModel), which correctly checks only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Manage-level operations on groups are authorized for callers that were only granted view permission.
raw_findings.impact: canManage() returns true when only the VIEW scope is granted because the hasPermission check accepts either scope, so a view-only admin can pass manage checks (e.g. create groups) — a privilege escalation. raw_findings.root_cause: Copy-paste of the canView() scope list (VIEW, MANAGE) into the canManage() evaluation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Change canManage() to return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) only, and align the new GroupPermissionEvaluator#canManage() javadoc (which currently documents 'VIEW or MANAGE') accordingly.
raw_findings.title: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage access from the VIEW scope

raw_findings.body: Previously canViewGlobal was computed once and short-circuited the filter. Now GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group) is invoked per group, and for role-less admins each call performs a resource-store lookup plus a full authorization policy evaluation (hasPermission fallback to the Groups type resource), turning one policy evaluation into N — a measurable latency/DB regression on group listing.
raw_findings.failure_mode: O(N) authorization engine evaluations per group listing request instead of O(1) for globally-permitted admins.
raw_findings.impact: Previously canViewGlobal was computed once and short-circuited the filter. Now GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group) is invoked per group, and for role-less admins each call performs a resource-store lookup plus a full authorization policy evaluation (hasPermission fallback to the Groups type resource), turning one policy evaluation into N — a measurable latency/DB regression on group listing.
raw_findings.root_cause: Refactor dropped the cached global permission check, relying on the per-group evaluator that performs a policy evaluation per element in V2.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Hoist a single groupsEvaluator.canView() check before the stream and only fall back to per-group canView(g) when the global check fails, as the previous code did.
raw_findings.title: Removed global canView() hoist causes per-group policy evaluation in GroupsResource.getGroups (V2)
raw_findings.trigger: With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, an admin whose group visibility comes from an all-groups VIEW/MANAGE permission (not admin roles) lists groups with populateHierarchy=false in a realm with many groups.

raw_findings.body: The removed canViewGlobal short-circuit means GroupPermissionsV2.canView(g) runs a resource lookup and authorization policy evaluation for every subgroup in the unpaginated stream, multiplying policy-engine work compared to the single global evaluation performed before.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Per-subgroup authorization evaluations on the full (pre-pagination) subgroup stream.
raw_findings.impact: The removed canViewGlobal short-circuit means GroupPermissionsV2.canView(g) runs a resource lookup and authorization policy evaluation for every subgroup in the unpaginated stream, multiplying policy-engine work compared to the single global evaluation performed before.
raw_findings.root_cause: Refactor dropped the cached global permission check in favor of a per-element evaluator call that is expensive in V2.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Compute auth.groups().canView() once and use it to short-circuit the per-group filter, matching the prior pattern.
raw_findings.title: Removed global canView() hoist causes per-subgroup policy evaluation in GroupResource.getSubGroups (V2)
raw_findings.trigger: With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, an admin whose visibility comes from an all-groups VIEW/MANAGE permission requests subgroups of a group with many children (getSubGroupsStream is fetched with -1/-1 before pagination).

raw_findings.body: Previously the feature was checked per event, so toggling the feature at runtime immediately affected cleanup behavior. Now, if the feature is disabled at registration time and enabled later, the role/client/group-removed cleanup of V1 permission objects never runs, leaving stale authorization policies/resources behind after entity deletion.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Removed roles/clients/groups leave orphaned fine-grained-permission objects when the feature state changes after startup.
raw_findings.impact: Previously the feature was checked per event, so toggling the feature at runtime immediately affected cleanup behavior. Now, if the feature is disabled at registration time and enabled later, the role/client/group-removed cleanup of V1 permission objects never runs, leaving stale authorization policies/resources behind after entity deletion.
raw_findings.root_cause: Hoisting the feature-flag check out of the event handler binds the decision to factory initialization time instead of event time.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep the Profile.isFeatureEnabled check inside onEvent (or document/guarantee that the feature state cannot change after session-factory initialization).
raw_findings.title: Feature check for AFGA listener moved from event time to registration time
raw_findings.trigger: registerListener runs during session-factory init; the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature state is changed afterwards without re-initializing the factory (runtime feature toggling used by the testsuite/embedded deployments, or Profile configured after factory init), then a role, client, or group is removed.

validated_findings.body: Group resources in V2 are named by group ID (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returning group.getId()), while getId() is the authz Resource's own UUID. hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) therefore never finds the per-group resource (findByName with a resource UUID returns null) and falls back to the all-groups check, and granted collects resource UUIDs rather than group IDs. Callers store this set in session attribute UserModel.GROUPS / pass it to getUsersCount, where the JPA group-membership subquery matches nothing — user counts return 0 and group-scoped searches return no users (or all groups' resource UUIDs when an all-groups policy exists), inconsistent with per-user canView evaluation.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Admins with per-group view-members/manage-members permissions get zero user counts and empty group-filtered user searches despite having access.
validated_findings.impact: Group resources in V2 are named by group ID (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returning group.getId()), while getId() is the authz Resource's own UUID. hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) therefore never finds the per-group resource (findByName with a resource UUID returns null) and falls back to the all-groups check, and granted collects resource UUIDs rather than group IDs. Callers store this set in session attribute UserModel.GROUPS / pass it to getUsersCount, where the JPA group-membership subquery matches nothing — user counts return 0 and group-scoped searches return no users (or all groups' resource UUIDs when an all-groups policy exists), inconsistent with per-user canView evaluation.
validated_findings.root_cause: Confusion between the authz Resource's generated ID and the Resource's name, which is the group ID in the V2 schema.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use groupResource.getName() (which holds the group ID) both as the argument to hasPermission(...) and as the value added to the granted set.
validated_findings.title: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes/collects authz resource IDs instead of group IDs
validated_findings.trigger: With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, an admin without global view-users permission is granted VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on a specific group, then calls a user count or search endpoint (UsersResource.getUsersCount / searchForUser, BruteForceUsersResource) that relies on getGroupIdsWithViewPermission().
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines R122-R123 show hasPermission(groupResource.getId(),...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). The V1 GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission at L313-315 uses resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length()) to extract the group ID. In V2, resolveGroup returns group.getId() as the resource name, but the code passes/collects groupResource.getId() (the authz Resource UUID) instead of groupResource.getName() (the group ID). This mismatch causes the returned set to contain wrong IDs.
